summary.text: Glenn Ivey is the Democratic incumbent in Maryland's 4th Congressional District. A lawyer and former federal prosecutor, he chaired the Maryland Public Service Commission and served two terms as Prince George's County State's Attorney before his 2022 election to Congress. He is seeking a third term.

paragraphs.text: Ivey was born in Chelsea, Massachusetts, in 1961 and, according to his congressional website, grew up in Rocky Mount, North Carolina, and Dale City, Virginia.
He graduated from Princeton University in 1983 (B.A. in politics) and Harvard Law School in 1986.

He began his legal career in the litigation department of the Baltimore firm Gordon, Feinblatt, Rothman, Hoffberger & Hollander and served as an Assistant U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia from 1990 to 1994.
On Capitol Hill, he worked as a legislative assistant to Rep. John Conyers, counsel to the Senate Whitewater Committee for Sen. Paul Sarbanes, and chief counsel to Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle.
He was later a partner at Preston, Gates, Ellis and at Venable, and taught as an adjunct law professor at the University of Maryland (1995-2014) and Harvard (2013-2021).
Gov. Parris Glendening appointed Ivey chairman of the Maryland Public Service Commission in 1998.

He was elected State's Attorney for Prince George's County in 2002 and served two consecutive terms; his congressional website cites a Domestic Violence Prosecution Unit and a mortgage fraud unit created during his tenure.
Ivey was elected to Congress in 2022 and sworn in in January 2023.
He served on the Judiciary and Homeland Security Committees in the 118th Congress and now serves on the Appropriations and Ethics Committees.

He won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 79.2% of the vote and, according to his congressional website, lives in Prince George's County with his wife, Jolene, a county councilmember; they have six children.
